Brentwood's population increased by around 3,400 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population passed 77,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Brentwood increased by 4.7%, from just over 73,600 in 2011 to around 77,000 in 2021.

The population here increased by a smaller percentage than the overall population of the East of England (8.3%), and by a smaller percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Brentwood was home to around 3.6 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 3.4 in 2011. This area was among the lowest 45% for population density across English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was lower in Brentwood than across the East of England

Median age in Brentwood

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Brentwood decreased by one year, from 43 to 42 years of age.

This area had a slightly higher average (median) age than the East of England as a whole in 2021 (41 years) and a higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 25 to 34 years rose by just over 1,800 (an increase of 22.6%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by just under 1,500 (8.9% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 25 and 34 years increased by 1.9 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Unpaid care in Brentwood

Brentwood saw the East of England's joint third-largest percentage-point fall (alongside Bedford, Cambridge and Babergh) in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care (from 7.9% in 2011 to 4.7% in 2021). These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

Across the region, only Rochford (from 8.0% to 4.7%) and Dacorum (from 8.0% to 4.7%) saw a greater decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care.

Every local authority area across the East of England saw a fall in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care, as the regional proportion fell from 7.3% to 4.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Brentwood decreased by 3.2 percentage points

Health in Brentwood

In 2021, 54.3% of Brentwood residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 50.9% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 33.6% to 31.9%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Brentwood residents describing their health as "very bad" remained 0.9%, while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 3.1% to 2.8%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very good health in Brentwood increased by 3.4 percentage points

Rise in private renting

Of Brentwood households, 16.0% rented privately in 2021, up from 11.3% in 2011.

The increase in the percentage of privately-rented homes was greater in Brentwood (4.7 percentage points) than across the East of England (3.5 percentage points, from 14.7% to 18.2%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.6 percentage points, from 16.8% to 20.5%.

Private renting in Brentwood increased by 4.7 percentage points

Religion in Brentwood

In 2021, 33.3% of Brentwood residents reported having "No religion", up from 21.1% in 2011. The rise of 12.2 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Brentwood. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the East of England, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 27.9% to 40.2%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 56.0% of people in Brentwood described themselves as Christian (down from 68.6%), while 5.6% did not state their religion (down from 7.1% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

In 2021, 33.3% of usual residents in Brentwood reported having "No religion"

Brentwood residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 67,100 Brentwood residents said they were born in England. This represented 87.1% of the local population. The figure has risen from around 66,000 in 2011, which at the time represented 89.6% of Brentwood's population.

India was the next most represented, with around 1,000 Brentwood residents reporting this country of birth (1.3%). This figure was up from just over 500 in 2011, which at the time represented 0.7% of the population of Brentwood.

The number of Brentwood residents born in Ireland fell from around 700 in 2011 (0.9% of the local population) to just over 650 in 2021 (0.9%).

In 2021, 87.1% of Brentwood residents reported their country of birth as England

National identity in Brentwood

In 2021, 5.7% of Brentwood residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 4.4% in 2011.

In 2021, 1.6% of residents identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 0.8% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Brentwood that identified as "British only" increased from 14.8% to 55.6%.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater across the East of England (2.1 percentage points, from 6.9% to 9.0%) than in Brentwood (1.3 percentage points). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Brentwood increased by 1.3 percentage points

Family in Brentwood

Of Brentwood households, 16.2% included a couple but no children in 2021, down from 17.1% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in five households (21.6%) included a couple with dependent children, compared with 22.2% in 2011. The percentage of single family households including a couple living with only non-dependent children remained at 7.7%.

The decrease in the percentage of households including a couple but no children was greater across the East of England (1.8 percentage points, from 19.0% to 17.2%) than in Brentwood (0.9 percentage points). Across England, the percentage fell by 0.9 percentage points, from 17.6% to 16.8%.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in Brentwood decreased by 0.9 percentage points

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of Brentwood residents aged 16 years and over, 33.9% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 29.6% in 2011.

In 2021, just under one in two people (48.9%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 52.2% in 2011. The percentage of adults in Brentwood that had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership increased from 8.4% to 8.6%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership was greater in Brentwood (4.2 percentage points) than across the East of England (3.7 percentage points, from 31.1% to 34.8%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.3 percentage points, from 34.6% to 37.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Brentwood increased by 4.2 percentage points

Employment in Brentwood

Of Brentwood residents aged 16 years and over, 59.3% said they were employed (excluding full-time students) in 2021, the same percentage as in 2011.

In 2021, just under 1 in 40 people (2.3%) said they were unemployed, compared with 2.8% in 2011. The percentage of retired Brentwood residents decreased from 23.9% to 23.7%.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed fell from 58.4% to 57.3% across the East of England. Across England, the percentage fell from 56.5% to 55.7%.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

In 2021, 59.3% of usual residents aged 16 years and over said they were employed (excluding full-time students) in Brentwood

Change in work hours

In 2021, 11.1% of Brentwood residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure increased from 10.4% in 2011.

In 2021, just over one in seven people (15.2%) said they worked over 49 hours per week, compared with 17.4% in 2011. The percentage of adults in employment working 31 to 48 hours per week increased from 55.1% to 57.4%.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week in Brentwood (0.7 percentage points) was similar to the increase across the East of England (0.4 percentage points, from 10.4% to 10.8%). Across England, the percentage increased by 0.6 percentage points, from 9.7% to 10.3%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Brentwood increased by 0.7 percentage points

Disability in Brentwood

In 2021, 5.4% of Brentwood residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 6.6% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, around 1 in 12 people (8.3%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 8.7% in 2011. The proportion of Brentwood residents who were not disabled increased from 84.7% to 86.3%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Brentwood (1.2 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the East of England (1.2 percentage points, from 7.8% to 6.6%). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Brentwood decreased by 1.2 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Brentwood

In 2021, 5.1% of Brentwood residents identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category, up from 3.2% in 2011. The 1.9 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the East of England, the percentage of people from the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" ethnic group increased from 4.8% to 6.4%, while across England the percentage increased from 7.8% to 9.6%.

In 2021, 88.5% of people in Brentwood identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 93.6% in 2011), while 3.1% identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category (compared with 1.6% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category increased from 1.2% in 2011 to 2.3% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.
